name: cloud-keyboard
description: Cloud Keyboard — HeliBoard IME with on-device translation, voice input, and bundled sticker packs. Standalone constellation APK.

android._doc_version: version_code/version_name live here, not in app/build.gradle. libs/keyboard is shared by reference and reads ${rootDir}/build.json, so these are what the keyboard APK's BuildConfig reports - they used to resolve to ea_cloud-superapp's because the module read a relative path.

libs:keyboard._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ea_cloud-superapp/libs/ - settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. These paths used to be hardcoded as include/projectDir pairs in settings.gradle, which meant the module graph lived in two places and neither knew about the other. build.json is now the only place a module is declared.

modules._doc: Keyboard libs are shared from ../ea_cloud-libs-shared/libs/ via relative project references in settings.gradle.

keyboard_media._doc: Same block as ea_cloud-superapp — shared vault secret. build.sh sops-decrypts vault_secrets → TENOR_API_KEY/GIPHY_API_KEY env vars → Gradle BuildConfig → MediaRuntime.configure().

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps — the SAME key that signs the superapp, so the in-app fleet updater never hits INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, and _enforce_signature re-signs the built APK with it. NO fallback: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD — it never signs with the ephemeral android debug keystore.
